locations.name: Kyiv
locations.description: Capital of Ukraine and seat of the Ukrainian government, targeted repeatedly by long-range Russian missile and drone strikes.

locations.name: Kharkiv
locations.description: Ukraine's second-largest city, near the northeastern border with Russia and under recurring artillery and glide-bomb range pressure.
locations.control: Held by Ukrainian forces; Russian forces are attempting to advance within artillery range of the city

locations.name: Kupiansk
locations.description: Kharkiv Oblast city on the Oskil River that changed hands early in the war and remains a contested infiltration front.
locations.control: Held by Ukrainian forces amid continued Russian infiltration attempts

locations.name: Pokrovsk
locations.description: Donetsk Oblast logistics hub and rail junction that has been a focal point of Russia's slow-moving offensive for over a year.
locations.control: Held by Ukrainian forces, who have repelled repeated Russian advances

locations.name: Zaporizhzhia
locations.description: Regional capital on the Dnipro River, near the front line since Russia's 2022 invasion of the surrounding oblast.
locations.control: Held by Ukrainian forces

locations.name: Kherson
locations.description: Southern regional capital on the west bank of the Dnipro, retaken by Ukraine in November 2022 and shelled from Russian-held territory across the river since.
locations.control: Held by Ukrainian forces west of the Dnipro River

locations.name: Mariupol
locations.description: Sea of Azov port city largely destroyed in a months-long 2022 siege and held by Russian forces since, now a rebuilt administrative center under occupation.

locations.name: Sevastopol
locations.description: Crimean port city and historic headquarters of Russia's Black Sea Fleet; Crimea has been administered by Russia since a 2014 annexation that most of the international community does not recognize.

locations.name: Odesa
locations.description: Ukraine's principal Black Sea port, essential to grain exports and a recurring target of Russian missile and drone strikes.

locations.name: Gaza City
locations.description: The Gaza Strip's largest city, in the north of the territory, heavily damaged during the 2023-2025 war and outside the Israeli-held Yellow Line zone.

locations.name: Khan Younis
locations.description: Southern Gaza's largest city, roughly bisected by the ceasefire's Yellow Line demarcation, with the two halves falling under differing zones of control.

locations.name: Rafah
locations.description: Southernmost Gaza city on the Egyptian border, most of which sits inside the Israeli-controlled Yellow Line zone under the current ceasefire.
locations.control: Israeli troops remain stationed at the Rafah border crossing after reopening it in February 2026

locations.name: Philadelphi Corridor
locations.description: Narrow strip along the Gaza-Egypt border historically used for smuggling tunnels and held by Israeli forces since 2024.

locations.name: Kerem Shalom Crossing
locations.description: The main commercial and humanitarian aid crossing between Israel and Gaza, near the Egyptian border tri-point.

locations.name: Rafah Crossing
locations.description: The principal crossing between Gaza and Egypt, used for aid deliveries and medical evacuations, subject to intermittent closure during the war.

locations.name: Erez Crossing
locations.description: Pedestrian crossing on Gaza's northern border with Israel, historically the main route for people movement between the territory and Israel.

locations.name: Ashkelon
locations.description: Israeli coastal city just north of the Gaza Strip, repeatedly targeted by rocket fire from Gaza-based armed groups during the war.

locations.name: Tehran
locations.description: Capital of Iran and seat of government, targeted during the February 2026 U.S. and Israeli strikes.
locations.control: Islamic Republic of Iran, under Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei since his father's death in February 2026

locations.name: Natanz
locations.description: Underground uranium enrichment facility in central Iran, one of three nuclear sites struck by U.S. forces on June 21, 2025.

locations.name: Fordow
locations.description: Fortified underground uranium enrichment site near Qom, struck alongside Natanz and Isfahan in the June 2025 U.S. strikes.

locations.name: Isfahan
locations.description: Major central Iranian city and site of a nuclear technology center struck by U.S. forces in June 2025.

locations.name: Strait of Hormuz
locations.description: Narrow maritime chokepoint between the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman through which a large share of global oil transits.
locations.control: Contested; Iranian forces attempted to close the strait during the 2026 war, met by a U.S. Navy blockade of Iranian ports

locations.name: Bandar Abbas
locations.description: Iran's principal naval base on the Strait of Hormuz, home port for its Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy.

locations.name: Bushehr
locations.description: Site of Iran's sole operating nuclear power plant, on the Persian Gulf coast.

locations.name: Tel Aviv
locations.description: Israel's commercial and diplomatic capital, repeatedly targeted by Iranian missile and drone strikes during the 2026 war.

locations.name: Al Udeid Air Base
locations.description: Qatari base hosting U.S. Central Command's forward headquarters, struck by Iranian missiles during the 2026 war.
locations.control: Qatari sovereign territory hosting U.S. forces; struck by Iran on June 23, 2025

locations.name: Beirut
locations.description: Capital of Lebanon and seat of the Lebanese government.

locations.name: Dahiyeh
locations.description: Hezbollah's traditional political and military stronghold in southern Beirut, repeatedly targeted by Israeli airstrikes during the war.

locations.name: Tyre
locations.description: Ancient port city in the heart of Hezbollah's south Lebanon base of support.

locations.name: Nabatieh
locations.description: South Lebanon provincial city struck repeatedly during the conflict, including reported strikes in July 2026.
locations.control: Outside formal Israeli-held zones but within range of continued Israeli strikes on Hezbollah-linked targets

locations.name: Naqoura
locations.description: Coastal town hosting the headquarters of the UN Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL), near the Israel-Lebanon border.

locations.name: Kfar Kila
locations.description: Border village directly on the Blue Line demarcation, among the areas hit hardest when the March 2026 ground invasion began.

locations.name: Litani River
locations.description: River roughly 30 kilometers north of the border that UN Security Council Resolution 1701 designates as the line behind which Hezbollah forces are meant to withdraw.

locations.name: Southern Lebanon buffer area
locations.description: Zone south of the Litani River where Israeli ground forces have operated since the March 2026 invasion.
locations.control: Israeli forces remain entrenched across roughly 20 percent of Lebanese territory, pending Hezbollah's disarmament under a June 2026 U.S.-brokered framework

locations.name: Sanaa
locations.description: Yemen's traditional capital, seized by Houthi forces in 2014 and still the seat of their administration.
locations.control: Houthi movement (Ansar Allah)

locations.name: Aden
locations.description: Southern port city serving as the interim seat of Yemen's internationally recognized government.
locations.control: Internationally recognized government (Presidential Leadership Council)

locations.name: Hodeidah
locations.description: Yemen's main Red Sea port and principal entry point for humanitarian aid, overlooking approaches to the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait.
locations.control: Houthi movement (Ansar Allah)

locations.name: Marib
locations.description: Oil- and gas-producing city east of Sanaa that has repeatedly repelled Houthi offensives and hosts large numbers of displaced Yemenis.

locations.name: Taiz
locations.description: Yemen's third-largest city, besieged and divided along front lines since 2015 with roads in and out subject to closure.

locations.name: Bab-el-Mandeb Strait
locations.description: Narrow maritime chokepoint between the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden through which a large share of global container traffic normally passes; repeatedly targeted by Houthi missile and drone attacks on shipping since late 2023.

locations.name: Al Mukha (Mocha)
locations.description: Historic Red Sea coffee-trade port south of Hodeidah that has changed hands multiple times during the war.

locations.name: Al Mukalla
locations.description: Main port of eastern Hadramawt governorate, briefly held by al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula in 2015-2016 before being retaken by a Saudi-led coalition offensive.

locations.name: Damascus
locations.description: Capital of Syria and seat of government since the Assad regime's collapse on December 8, 2024.
locations.control: Syrian Transitional Government (HTS-led)

locations.name: Aleppo
locations.description: Syria's largest city by pre-war population and an industrial hub in the north; the first major city taken in the offensive that toppled the Assad government.
locations.control: Syrian Transitional Government (HTS-led)

locations.name: Qamishli
locations.description: Largest city in Syria's Kurdish-majority northeast and former de facto capital of the Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria.
locations.control: Syrian government (administrative control transferred from the Syrian Democratic Forces under a US-mediated ceasefire reached January 30, 2026)

locations.name: Al-Hasakah
locations.description: Provincial capital in Syria's northeast, near oil fields and a former US military presence supporting the Syrian Democratic Forces.

locations.name: Homs
locations.description: Central Syrian crossroads city linking Damascus, the coast, and the north; a key strategic corridor since the war's start in 2011.

locations.name: Idlib
locations.description: Northwestern city that served as the last major opposition-held stronghold and the launch point for the late-2024 offensive against the Assad government.

locations.name: Latakia
locations.description: Mediterranean port city and historic base of Assad-family and Alawite support; site of serious sectarian violence in the months after the government's fall.

locations.name: Quneitra / Golan buffer zone
locations.description: Area along the Syria-Israel frontier near the Golan Heights ceasefire line.
locations.control: Israeli military, operating a de facto buffer zone established December 8, 2024

locations.name: Tartus
locations.description: Syria's second Mediterranean port and the site of Russia's only overseas naval facility, leased since the Soviet era.

locations.name: Baghdad
locations.description: Capital of Iraq and seat of the federal government, currently led by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi.

locations.name: Mosul
locations.description: Iraq's second-largest city, captured by the Islamic State in June 2014 and recaptured by Iraqi forces in July 2017.

locations.name: Kirkuk
locations.description: Oil-rich city that sits along the fault line between Iraq's Kurdistan autonomous region and areas administered by the federal government, a longstanding source of Arab-Kurdish tension.

locations.name: Erbil
locations.description: Capital of the Kurdistan Regional Government in northern Iraq.

locations.name: Basra
locations.description: Iraq's main port city and oil-export hub on the Persian Gulf.

locations.name: Al-Asad Airbase
locations.description: Major air base in western Anbar province used by U.S. forces in an advisory role against Islamic State remnants.
locations.control: Iraqi government, hosting roughly 2,500 U.S. troops in an advisory capacity

locations.name: Fallujah
locations.description: Anbar province city recaptured from the Islamic State in June 2016 after months of fighting.

locations.name: Ramadi
locations.description: Anbar province's capital, recaptured from the Islamic State in December 2015.

locations.name: Ankara
locations.description: Capital of Turkey and seat of the government negotiating the PKK peace and disarmament process.

locations.name: Diyarbakir
locations.description: Largest Kurdish-majority city in southeastern Turkey and a center of Kurdish political life.

locations.name: Qandil Mountains
locations.description: Mountainous range in Iraqi Kurdistan near the Iran border that has served as the PKK's main base area for decades.
locations.control: Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) operational base, though the group announced its intent to disarm and disband in 2025

locations.name: Sinjar
locations.description: Yazidi-majority district in northern Iraq where Turkey has conducted strikes against PKK-linked forces.

locations.name: Imrali Island
locations.description: Sea of Marmara prison island holding PKK founder Abdullah Ocalan, who called for the group's disbandment in February 2025.

locations.name: Zakho
locations.description: Iraqi Kurdistan border town near Turkish military outposts established under Turkey's cross-border Operation Claw campaign.

locations.name: Kobani
locations.description: Syrian border city that became a symbol of Kurdish YPG resistance against the Islamic State and a recurring flashpoint in Turkey-Syria tensions.

locations.name: Qamishli
locations.description: Largest city in Syria's Kurdish-majority northeast, whose SDF forces signed an accord to integrate with Syria's post-Assad armed forces after 2024.

locations.name: Khartoum
locations.description: Sudan's capital, the site of the war's opening battles in April 2023 and heavily damaged before its recapture from the Rapid Support Forces.
locations.control: Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF)

locations.name: Omdurman
locations.description: Khartoum's twin city across the Nile, retaken from Rapid Support Forces in early 2025 fighting.
locations.control: Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF)

locations.name: El Fasher
locations.description: Capital of North Darfur and the army's last major stronghold in the region until it fell after an eighteen-month siege on October 27, 2025.
locations.control: Rapid Support Forces (RSF)

locations.name: Port Sudan
locations.description: Red Sea port city that has functioned as the wartime seat of Sudan's government and its main gateway for humanitarian and commercial shipping.

locations.name: El Obeid
locations.description: North Kordofan capital with rail links to Khartoum, held after the army broke a Rapid Support Forces siege in February 2025.
locations.control: Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF)

locations.name: Nyala
locations.description: Largest city in South Darfur and a commercial hub for the wider Darfur region.

locations.name: El Geneina
locations.description: Capital of West Darfur, near the Chad border, the site of mass ethnically targeted killings documented early in the war.

locations.name: Kadugli
locations.description: Capital of South Kordofan, a state that has seen fighting spread as the conflict's east-west front line hardens.

locations.name: Juba
locations.description: South Sudan's capital and seat of the Transitional Government, briefly threatened by fighting in early 2025 before Ugandan forces deployed in support.
locations.control: South Sudan's Transitional Government, held with the support of SSPDF and allied Ugandan forces deployed in 2025

locations.name: Akobo
locations.description: Eastern Jonglei town near the Ethiopian border where fighting in 2025-2026 displaced civilians.
locations.control: South Sudan People's Defence Forces (SSPDF), which took the town in early March 2026

locations.name: Nasir
locations.description: Upper Nile town on the Sobat River where an army base was overrun during the White Army's 2025 offensive, a flashpoint in the collapse of the unity government.

locations.name: Malakal
locations.description: Capital of Upper Nile state and a historic front line of South Sudan's civil wars, sited on the Nile's main river-transport corridor.

locations.name: Bentiu
locations.description: Capital of oil-producing Unity state, repeatedly fought over since 2013 for its proximity to South Sudan's main oil fields.

locations.name: Bor
locations.description: Capital of Jonglei state and site of a 2013 massacre that marked the civil war's opening phase.

locations.name: Wau
locations.description: Capital of Western Bahr el Ghazal state and South Sudan's second-largest city, a rail and road hub in the country's west.

locations.name: Renk
locations.description: Border town on the Sudan frontier that serves as the main transit point for people fleeing both South Sudan's conflict and the war in Sudan.

locations.name: Yei
locations.description: Southern town near the Ugandan border, an agricultural center and displacement corridor for South Sudanese fleeing violence.

locations.name: Mogadishu
locations.description: Somalia's capital and largest city, seat of the Federal Government, which has repeatedly been the target of al-Shabaab bombings and assaults.
locations.control: Federal Government of Somalia

locations.name: Kismayo
locations.description: Jubaland's capital and southern Somalia's principal port, al-Shabaab's last major urban stronghold until government-aligned forces retook it in October 2012.

locations.name: Baidoa
locations.description: Capital of South West State and a frequent staging point for government and African Union operations against al-Shabaab in the surrounding Bay region.

locations.name: Beledweyne
locations.description: Hiiraan region capital where government forces made significant gains against al-Shabaab during the 2022-2023 central Somalia offensive.

locations.name: Jowhar
locations.description: Capital of Hirshabelle state on the Shabelle River, a farming region contested during successive government offensives against al-Shabaab.

locations.name: Baraawe
locations.description: Historic Indian Ocean port south of Mogadishu that has changed hands between government and al-Shabaab forces over the course of the conflict.

locations.name: Bosaso
locations.description: Puntland's main commercial port on the Gulf of Aden, largely insulated from the al-Shabaab insurgency further south.

locations.name: Garoowe
locations.description: Capital of the semi-autonomous Puntland state in northeastern Somalia.

locations.name: Addis Ababa
locations.description: Ethiopia's capital and seat of the federal government, increasingly within reach of Oromo Liberation Army activity spreading from Oromia region.
locations.control: Federal government of Ethiopia (Ethiopian National Defense Force)

locations.name: Mekelle
locations.description: Capital of Tigray region, administered by a federally appointed Interim Administration after the 2022 peace deal until renewed clashes in 2026.
locations.control: Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) / Tigray Defense Forces, which took effective control from the Interim Administration after clashes in 2026

locations.name: Bahir Dar
locations.description: Capital of Amhara region on Lake Tana, a target of offensives by the Fano militia insurgency active across the region since 2023.

locations.name: Shire
locations.description: Northwestern Tigray town that has served as a major shelter site for civilians displaced by the region's recurring rounds of conflict.

locations.name: Humera
locations.description: Town anchoring the disputed Western Tigray territory, occupied by Amhara regional and Eritrean forces since the Tigray war and claimed by both Tigray and Amhara.

locations.name: Jijiga
locations.description: Capital of Ethiopia's Somali region, on the road corridor linking Addis Ababa to the port of Berbera in Somaliland.

locations.name: Ambo
locations.description: Oromia town west of Addis Ababa that has repeatedly seen unrest tied to the Oromo Liberation Army insurgency.

locations.name: Gondar
locations.description: Historic former imperial capital in Amhara region and a center of Fano militia recruitment and activity.

locations.name: Goma
locations.description: Capital of North Kivu province and eastern DRC's largest city, on the Rwandan border, captured by M23 in January 2025.
locations.control: M23, backed by Rwandan forces

locations.name: Bukavu
locations.description: Capital of South Kivu province on Lake Kivu, seized by M23 in February 2025 shortly after the fall of Goma.
locations.control: M23, backed by Rwandan forces

locations.name: Kinshasa
locations.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo's capital, on the Congo River in the far west of the country, seat of President Félix Tshisekedi's government.
locations.control: Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo

locations.name: Kisangani
locations.description: Major Congo River port city in the country's northeast interior, a historic strategic prize in successive Congolese conflicts.

locations.name: Beni
locations.description: North Kivu city near the Ugandan border that has been a recurring target of attacks attributed to the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF).

locations.name: Butembo
locations.description: Commercial hub in North Kivu province, north of Goma, situated amid overlapping armed-group activity in the eastern Congo conflict zone.

locations.name: Uvira
locations.description: South Kivu town on Lake Tanganyika near the Burundian border, a strategic gateway between eastern DRC and the African Great Lakes region.

locations.name: Kasindi
locations.description: Main official border crossing between North Kivu and Uganda, a key commercial trade route into eastern DRC.

locations.name: Bangui
locations.description: Capital of the Central African Republic on the Ubangi River, seat of the government and site of a July 2025 ceremony marking a ceasefire with armed groups.
locations.control: Central African Republic government forces, alongside Russian security personnel (Wagner/Africa Corps) and UN MINUSCA peacekeepers

locations.name: Birao
locations.description: Remote capital of Vakaga prefecture in the far northeast, near the borders with Chad and Sudan, historically difficult for the state to secure.

locations.name: Bria
locations.description: Capital of Haute-Kotto prefecture and a diamond-mining center that has repeatedly been contested by armed factions competing for mining revenue.

locations.name: Bambari
locations.description: Central Ouaka prefecture capital and one of the country's larger interior towns, a historic base for former Seleka factions.

locations.name: Bangassou
locations.description: Southeastern town on the Mbomou River across from the Democratic Republic of Congo, a cross-border trade and displacement route.

locations.name: Paoua
locations.description: Northwestern town that was a longtime stronghold of the 3R armed group before its 2025 ceasefire and dissolution.

locations.name: Berberati
locations.description: Southwestern regional center near the Cameroonian border, a commercial hub for the country's timber-producing region.

locations.name: Maiduguri
locations.description: Capital of Borno state and the birthplace of Boko Haram in 2002, now the most fortified city in the northeast and headquarters of Nigeria's counterinsurgency operations.

locations.name: Chibok
locations.description: Borno town where Boko Haram abducted a large group of schoolgirls in April 2014, an attack that drew global attention to the insurgency.

locations.name: Sambisa Forest
locations.description: Dense forest reserve in southern Borno state that served as a historic Boko Haram base and hideout for abducted captives.

locations.name: Gwoza
locations.description: Borno town near the Cameroonian border and the Mandara Mountains, the site of hostage releases by Boko Haram in mid-2026.

locations.name: Baga
locations.description: Fishing town on the Nigerian shore of Lake Chad that has repeatedly been fought over by Boko Haram/ISWAP factions and Nigerian and multinational forces.

locations.name: Abuja
locations.description: Nigeria's federal capital, targeted by a Boko Haram bus-station bombing in 2014 and the seat of national counterterrorism policy.

locations.name: Damaturu
locations.description: Capital of Yobe state, one of the three northeastern states placed under a state of emergency in 2013 as the insurgency escalated.

locations.name: Lake Chad Basin
locations.description: Shrinking inland lake shared by Nigeria, Chad, Niger, and Cameroon whose islands and shoreline have been repeatedly contested between Boko Haram's JAS and ISWAP factions.

locations.name: Bamako
locations.description: Capital of Mali and seat of the military government that has led the country since a series of coups beginning in 2020.

locations.name: Timbuktu
locations.description: Historic northern Mali city that was blockaded by JNIM militants in 2023, cutting off fuel and food supplies to the population.

locations.name: Gao
locations.description: Major city in northern Mali on the Niger River, a longtime hub for French, UN, and now Russian military operations in the region.

locations.name: Niamey
locations.description: Capital of Niger and seat of the military government installed by the 2023 coup that ended Western security cooperation with France and the United States.

locations.name: Ouagadougou
locations.description: Capital of Burkina Faso and seat of the military government that has governed the country since the 2022 coups.

locations.name: Liptako-Gourma borderlands
locations.description: Tri-border region where Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger meet, the epicenter of the JNIM and Islamic State Sahel Province insurgencies and a large share of global terrorism-related deaths.

locations.name: Markoye
locations.description: Northern Burkina Faso town near the Malian and Nigerien borders that has repeatedly been the site of attacks attributed to Islamic State Sahel Province.

locations.name: Diffa
locations.description: Southeastern Niger city near Lake Chad and the Nigerian border, at the intersection of the Sahel insurgency and the Boko Haram/ISWAP conflict.

locations.name: Pemba
locations.description: Capital of Cabo Delgado province and the region's main port and administrative center for the counterinsurgency campaign.

locations.name: Mocímboa da Praia
locations.description: Coastal town seized by Islamic State Mozambique insurgents at the peak of their 2020 offensive and retaken by Mozambican and Rwandan forces in 2021.
locations.control: Mozambican Armed Forces (FADM) and Rwanda Defence Force troops hold the town, though Islamic State Mozambique continues to mount IED and raid attacks nearby

locations.name: Palma
locations.description: Northern coastal town near Mozambique's offshore natural gas fields, the site of a major Islamic State Mozambique attack in March 2021 that halted LNG development.

locations.name: Macomia
locations.description: Cabo Delgado district town that has seen recurring Islamic State Mozambique activity, including IED deployments in 2026.
locations.control: Mozambican state forces hold the town center, while Islamic State Mozambique operates from forest bases in the surrounding district

locations.name: Mueda
locations.description: Plateau town hosting one of the main Mozambican and allied military garrisons supporting operations across northern Cabo Delgado.

locations.name: Nangade
locations.description: District bordering Tanzania that has seen clashes between Islamic State Mozambique insurgents and Mozambican and Rwandan forces.

locations.name: Quissanga
locations.description: Coastal district south of Mocímboa da Praia used by Islamic State Mozambique as a transit route between operational areas.

locations.name: Montepuez
locations.description: Inland town known for ruby mining that has become a major host site for civilians displaced by the Cabo Delgado insurgency.

locations.name: Tripoli
locations.description: Capital of Libya and seat of the UN-recognized Government of National Unity (GNU).
locations.control: Government of National Unity (GNU), led by Prime Minister Abdul Hamid Dbeibah, with Turkish military support

locations.name: Benghazi
locations.description: Libya's second-largest city and historic base of Khalifa Haftar's Libyan National Army.
locations.control: Libyan National Army (LNA), aligned with the eastern-based House of Representatives government

locations.name: Sirte
locations.description: Central coastal city that changed hands repeatedly during the war against the Islamic State and now serves as the seat of the eastern House of Representatives government.
locations.control: House of Representatives (HoR) government, backed by the Libyan National Army

locations.name: Misrata
locations.description: Major western port city and stronghold of militias aligned with the Tripoli-based government.

locations.name: Derna
locations.description: Eastern coastal city and the Islamic State's last stronghold in Libya until its recapture by the LNA in July 2018.

locations.name: Sabha
locations.description: Largest city in Libya's southern Fezzan region, a hub for cross-border smuggling routes and foreign-fighter presence.

locations.name: Zawiya
locations.description: Western coastal city near Tripoli with a major oil refinery and export terminal.

locations.name: Es Sider
locations.description: One of Libya's largest oil export terminals, repeatedly blockaded by rival factions to cut off opponents' revenue.

locations.name: Kabul
locations.description: Capital of Afghanistan, captured by the Taliban on August 15, 2021.
locations.control: Taliban (Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan)

locations.name: Kandahar
locations.description: Southern city that serves as the Taliban's spiritual and political heartland.

locations.name: Herat
locations.description: Major western Afghan city near the Iran border and a historic trade hub.

locations.name: Mazar-i-Sharif
locations.description: Largest city in northern Afghanistan and a former stronghold of anti-Taliban forces before 2021.

locations.name: Durand Line
locations.description: Contested colonial-era border dividing Pashtun tribal lands between Afghanistan and Pakistan, the site of repeated cross-border clashes since October 2025.

locations.name: Torkham
locations.description: Main Afghanistan-Pakistan border crossing on the historic Khyber Pass route, repeatedly closed during 2025-2026 clashes.

locations.name: Spin Boldak
locations.description: Southern Afghan border town opposite Pakistan's Chaman, another key crossing point affected by cross-border fighting.

locations.name: Panjshir Valley
locations.description: Mountainous valley northeast of Kabul and historic center of anti-Taliban resistance.

locations.name: Islamabad
locations.description: Capital of Pakistan and seat of the federal government, the site of a mosque suicide bombing on February 6, 2026.

locations.name: Peshawar
locations.description: Capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, near the Afghan border and a frequent target of Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) attacks.

locations.name: Quetta
locations.description: Capital of Balochistan province, a center of Baloch separatist insurgent activity.

locations.name: Karachi
locations.description: Pakistan's largest city and principal seaport on the Arabian Sea.

locations.name: Bajaur
locations.description: Tribal district near the Afghan border, the site of a Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan assault reported on February 17, 2026.

locations.name: Torkham
locations.description: Main Pakistan-Afghanistan border crossing on the Khyber Pass route, a recurring flashpoint in cross-border clashes.

locations.name: Chaman
locations.description: Balochistan border town opposite Afghanistan's Spin Boldak, another key crossing affected by the conflict.

locations.name: Gwadar
locations.description: Strategic deep-water Arabian Sea port developed with Chinese investment, in a Balochistan region affected by separatist attacks.

locations.name: Srinagar
locations.description: Summer capital of Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir.
locations.control: Government of India, administered as a union territory since the 2019 revocation of Article 370

locations.name: Muzaffarabad
locations.description: Capital of Pakistan-administered Azad Kashmir.
locations.control: Government of Pakistan, as capital of Azad Jammu and Kashmir

locations.name: Jammu
locations.description: Winter capital of Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir, south of the Kashmir Valley.

locations.name: Line of Control
locations.description: De facto military boundary dividing Kashmir between India and Pakistan, established under the 1972 Simla Agreement.

locations.name: Pahalgam
locations.description: Southern Kashmir town near which an April 2025 militant attack on tourists triggered the most serious India-Pakistan military confrontation since 2019.

locations.name: Gilgit
locations.description: Capital of Pakistan-administered Gilgit-Baltistan, a mountainous northern region bordering China.

locations.name: Siachen Glacier
locations.description: High-altitude glacier in eastern Kashmir disputed between India and Pakistan, site of the world's highest-altitude military standoff.

locations.name: Kargil
locations.description: Ladakh town near the Line of Control, site of the 1999 Kargil War between India and Pakistan.

locations.name: Naypyidaw
locations.description: Purpose-built administrative capital of Myanmar since 2005 and seat of the military-led government.

locations.name: Yangon
locations.description: Myanmar's largest city and commercial hub, a former capital retained as the country's principal port and business center.

locations.name: Mandalay
locations.description: Myanmar's second-largest city and a former royal capital in the central dry zone.

locations.name: Lashio
locations.description: Northern Shan State city and site of a regional military command headquarters seized in an August 2024 offensive.
locations.control: Myanmar National Democratic Alliance Army (MNDAA)

locations.name: Maungdaw
locations.description: Rakhine State township on the Bangladesh border, at the center of the 2017 Rohingya displacement crisis.
locations.control: Arakan Army

locations.name: Myawaddy
locations.description: Border town on the Moei River opposite Thailand, a key overland trade crossing and route for migrants and refugees.

locations.name: Sittwe
locations.description: Capital of Rakhine State and a Bay of Bengal port, home to a deep-sea port project and long-running displacement camps.

locations.name: Laukkai
locations.description: Administrative center of the Kokang Self-Administered Zone on the China border, historically a hub for cross-border trade and gambling operations.

locations.name: Taipei
locations.description: Capital of Taiwan and seat of its government, site of then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi's August 2022 visit that sharply raised cross-strait tensions.

locations.name: Kaohsiung
locations.description: Taiwan's largest port and a major naval base on the island's southwest coast.

locations.name: Kinmen Islands
locations.description: Taiwan-administered islands lying just a few kilometers off the mainland Chinese coast, the site of armed confrontations during the 1954-55 and 1958 Taiwan Strait crises.

locations.name: Matsu Islands
locations.description: Taiwan-administered island group near Fuzhou on the Chinese mainland, garrisoned as a forward defense position.

locations.name: Penghu Islands
locations.description: Taiwan-administered archipelago roughly midway across the Taiwan Strait, used as a staging area for military exercises.

locations.name: Pratas Island (Dongsha)
locations.description: Remote Taiwan-administered atoll in the northern South China Sea garrisoned by the Coast Guard Administration, considered a possible target for a Chinese pressure campaign short of a full invasion.

locations.name: Xiamen
locations.description: Mainland Chinese port city directly across the strait from Kinmen, used as a staging area for PLA exercises near Taiwan-held islands.

locations.name: Taiwan Strait median line
locations.description: Informal midpoint boundary between Taiwan and mainland China that Chinese military aircraft crossed only rarely before 2022 but now cross on a near-daily basis.
locations.control: Routinely crossed by PLA aircraft and vessels; no longer functions as an operational boundary

mainTheaters: 스카버러 암초, 세컨드 토마스 암초, 스프래틀리 군도

locations.name: Scarborough Shoal
locations.description: Reef claimed by both China and the Philippines, roughly 220 km from the Philippine coast; the scene of a 2012 standoff and repeated clashes since, including three incidents in a single week in July 2026.
locations.control: China maintains a de facto coast guard presence since the 2012 standoff; the Philippines continues to assert its claim

locations.name: Second Thomas Shoal (Ayungin)
locations.description: Reef within the Philippines' claimed exclusive economic zone where a deliberately grounded Philippine navy ship, BRP Sierra Madre, maintains a small garrison; the site of a June 17, 2026 vessel collision.
locations.control: Philippines maintains a military outpost via the grounded BRP Sierra Madre; China Coast Guard vessels conduct regular harassment patrols nearby

locations.name: Woody Island (Yongxing)
locations.description: Largest of the Paracel Islands, administered by China as the seat of Sansha City.
locations.control: China, which has militarized the island with fighter jets, cruise missiles, and a radar system

locations.name: Mischief Reef
locations.description: Reef in the Spratly Islands, within the Philippines' claimed exclusive economic zone, where an artificial island with a military-capable airstrip has been built.

locations.name: Fiery Cross Reef
locations.description: Reef in the Spratly Islands developed into an artificial island with an airstrip, radar, and other military facilities.

locations.name: Itu Aba (Taiping Island)
locations.description: Largest naturally occurring island in the Spratly group, administered by Taiwan and garrisoned by its Coast Guard Administration.

locations.name: Palawan
locations.description: Philippine island province closest to the contested Spratly Islands, host to Philippine naval facilities that support resupply missions to outlying garrisons.

locations.name: Subic Bay
locations.description: Former US naval base on Luzon now used as a Philippine military and commercial port, increasingly hosting joint exercises with US and allied forces amid South China Sea tensions.

locations.name: Yerevan
locations.description: Capital of Armenia and seat of its government.

locations.name: Baku
locations.description: Capital of Azerbaijan and seat of its government.

locations.name: Stepanakert (Khankendi)
locations.description: Former capital of the self-declared Republic of Artsakh, the area's ethnic Armenian population having largely left following Azerbaijan's September 2023 offensive.
locations.control: Azerbaijan, following the dissolution of the breakaway Nagorno-Karabakh administration

locations.name: Shusha (Shushi)
locations.description: Historic hilltop town overlooking Stepanakert, captured by Azerbaijani forces during the 2020 Nagorno-Karabakh war.
locations.control: Azerbaijan

locations.name: Nakhchivan
locations.description: Capital of the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic, an Azerbaijani exclave separated from mainland Azerbaijan by Armenian territory.

locations.name: Meghri / Zangezur corridor route
locations.description: Southernmost Armenian town along the route of a proposed transit corridor that would link mainland Azerbaijan to the Nakhchivan exclave through Armenia's Syunik province; construction was planned to begin in 2026.

locations.name: Tavush border region
locations.description: Undemarcated stretch of the Armenia-Azerbaijan frontier that has seen periodic border clashes and is subject to an ongoing demarcation process.

locations.name: Goris
locations.description: Armenian town in Syunik province that became a main reception point for ethnic Armenians leaving Nagorno-Karabakh in 2023.

locations.name: Mexico City
locations.description: Capital of Mexico and seat of the federal government directing national security policy against organized crime.

locations.name: Culiacan
locations.description: Capital of Sinaloa state and the historic home base of the Sinaloa Cartel.

locations.name: Guadalajara
locations.description: Capital of Jalisco state, the region long associated with the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG), led for years by Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes ('El Mencho').

locations.name: Tijuana
locations.description: Border city opposite San Diego and one of the world's busiest land border crossings, a longtime smuggling corridor into the United States.

locations.name: Ciudad Juarez
locations.description: Border city opposite El Paso, Texas, and a major crossing point that saw some of Mexico's worst cartel-related violence in the late 2000s and early 2010s.

locations.name: Acapulco
locations.description: Pacific resort port in Guerrero state; surrounding mountain areas of the state saw cartel attacks displace hundreds of families in 2026.

locations.name: Nuevo Laredo
locations.description: Border city opposite Laredo, Texas, and Mexico's busiest land freight crossing, long contested as a trafficking corridor.

locations.name: Puerto Vallarta
locations.description: Pacific coast resort city in Jalisco that saw coordinated arson, roadblocks, and lockdowns in a wave of retaliatory cartel violence in February 2026.

locations.name: Bogota
locations.description: Capital of Colombia and seat of its government.

locations.name: Tibu
locations.description: Municipality in the Catatumbo region of Norte de Santander, near the Venezuelan border, at the center of an armed-group offensive that displaced a large number of civilians beginning in January 2025.
locations.control: National Liberation Army (ELN), fighting to displace FARC dissident factions descended from the demobilized 33rd Front

locations.name: Cucuta
locations.description: Capital of Norte de Santander and a major crossing point on the Colombia-Venezuela border, a gateway to the conflict-affected Catatumbo region.

locations.name: Tumaco
locations.description: Pacific port in Nariño department near the Ecuadorian border, a longstanding hub for cocaine trafficking and a zone of competition among armed groups.

locations.name: Buenaventura
locations.description: Colombia's principal Pacific port, handling the bulk of the country's maritime trade and a recurring site of armed-group extortion and turf disputes.

locations.name: Quibdo
locations.description: Capital of Choco department, a Pacific lowland region with a strong presence of multiple armed and criminal groups competing over river and coastal trafficking routes.

locations.name: Arauca
locations.description: Capital of Arauca department on the Venezuelan border, a region with a long-established ELN presence.

locations.name: Puerto Asis
locations.description: Municipality in Putumayo department near the Ecuadorian border, in a coca-growing region with a history of competition among armed groups.

locations.name: Port-au-Prince
locations.description: Capital of Haiti and seat of its government, largely emptied of state authority as armed gangs expanded through the city after 2023.
locations.control: Armed gangs hold an estimated 90 percent of the city

locations.name: Petion-Ville
locations.description: Hillside suburb overlooking Port-au-Prince that historically housed much of the capital's wealthier population and foreign missions.

locations.name: Cite Soleil
locations.description: Densely populated waterfront district of Port-au-Prince long associated with gang activity and among the areas hardest hit by the current crisis.

locations.name: Varreux fuel terminal
locations.description: Main fuel import terminal serving Port-au-Prince, blockaded by armed groups during a 2021-2022 fuel crisis that paralyzed much of the capital.

locations.name: Cap-Haitien
locations.description: Haiti's second-largest city and a northern port that has functioned as a relatively more stable hub as violence concentrated in the capital.

locations.name: Gonaives
locations.description: Artibonite department city known as the birthplace of Haitian independence, in a region increasingly affected by expanding gang activity.

locations.name: Port-de-Paix
locations.description: Northern coastal city and departmental capital on Haiti's Tortuga Channel.

locations.name: Jeremie
locations.description: Port city on Haiti's southern peninsula, comparatively less affected by gang violence than the capital region.

locations.name: Quito
locations.description: Capital of Ecuador and seat of its government.

locations.name: Guayaquil
locations.description: Ecuador's largest city and principal port, accounting for roughly a quarter of the country's recorded gang violence events.
locations.control: Contested among multiple gangs, including Los Lobos, Los Tiguerones, Los Fenix, and Los Igualitos

locations.name: Duran
locations.description: City adjacent to Guayaquil with one of Ecuador's highest homicide rates, part of the gang-related violence surge that led to a nationwide state of emergency in 2023.

locations.name: Esmeraldas
locations.description: Northern Pacific port near the Colombian border, one of the coastal provinces where the bulk of Ecuador's recorded gang violence has concentrated.

locations.name: Manta
locations.description: Major Pacific fishing and container port in Manabi province, a coastal region affected by rising gang violence since 2024.

locations.name: Lago Agrio (Nueva Loja)
locations.description: Capital of Sucumbios province near the Colombian border, in an oil-producing Amazon region where gang presence has expanded alongside illegal mining and cross-border trafficking.

locations.name: Tulcan
locations.description: Ecuadorian border city on the crossing to Colombia's Nariño department.

locations.name: Huaquillas
locations.description: Ecuador's principal land border crossing with Peru, a route used for both legal trade and smuggling.
